metadata.title: A Magnificent Penthouse on Madison Square Park | Open House TV
metadata.description:
We're checking out a massive triplex penthouse in Manhattan's Flatiron neighborhood. With four exposures, iconic views are framed by the elegant arched windows at every turn. While the majestic interiors never fail to impress, it's the two huge terraces that really make this home stand out. With over 10,000 square feet of interior space and 5,730 of terraces, this home is truly a mansion in the sky.

Subscribe to Open House TV on YOUTUBE: bit.ly/openhouseyoutubesub
Open House TV INSTAGRAM: https://bit.ly/2T0aorL
Open House TV TWITTER: https://bit.ly/2szkqEX
Open House TV FACEBOOK: https://bit.ly/2TXSztC

Hi. I'm Mara Flash Blum from Sotheby's International Realty, and I'm here to welcome you to the most extraordinary penthouse nestled between two of the world's iconic buildings, the Empire State Building to the north and the Flatiron Building to the south. We are here in the heart of New York City, in the crown penthouse of 212 Fifth Avenue. There's a lot to see, so let the tour begin. 

This room is the epitome of elegance where you can entertain in a truly opulent style. The first thing you notice are these amazing arched windows and the landmark views that surround you. And with all this natural light, you can appreciate the exquisite design details. 

What's really special about this penthouse is its timeless beauty. Built in 1912, this home retains all its pre-war charm, but now with a modern aesthetic. For example, the fireplace is flanked with book-matched marble from Italy. The clean lines of the fireplace play nicely with the chevron pattern in the floors. And did I mention the gargoyles? 

Dine with an awe-inspiring view of the Empire State Building through this grand arch window. But there's plenty to see on the inside. This elegant pass-through fireplace mirrors the one in the living room, bathing your guests in the warm glow of a beautiful flame. And speaking of warm glow, this Fendi light fixture is my favorite. Are you ready to host a spectacular dinner party? 

The master suite is comprised of many rooms. The master bedroom, the sitting room, and the lounge area. This area also includes a gallery foyer, a breakfast bar, plus the sumptuous master bath. It 

Includes a steam shower, two marble vanities, a soaking tub, a bronze casement window, and a surprise view. With western exposure and complete privacy, you would never want to leave. Except, there's more to see. No detail has been overlooked, including the custom-designed bronze staircase that sweeps up to the observatory. 

The second level features a game room with a skylight and walls of glass, and an outdoor oasis that's a city block long. But there's one more place I have to show you. 

And to finish off the tour, take in the breathtaking views of the greatest city in the world. I hope you've enjoyed this look at 212 Fifth Avenue, a penthouse like no other.

summary.brief: A realtor in a red dress walks through a massive New York penthouse, showcasing its arched windows, terraces and luxury interiors.
summary.detailed: The video opens with an “Open House” logo over a city photograph, then introduces Mara Flash Blum of Sotheby’s International Realty. She begins a walkthrough of a four‑exposure, triplex penthouse at 212 Fifth Avenue that spans over 10,000 sq ft and contains five bedrooms. In the grand living room she highlights the soaring arched windows, the view of the Empire State Building, a fireplace flanked by Italian book‑matched marble, chevron‑patterned floors and decorative gargoyles, as well as a Fendi light fixture. From the balcony she shows a white sofa and sweeping skyline vistas. She moves to a dining area with a matching pass‑through fireplace and describes the space as perfect for hosting. The tour continues through the master suite, which includes a bedroom, sitting room, lounge, gallery foyer, breakfast bar and a lavish master bath with a steam shower, marble vanities, a soaking tub and a bronze casement window offering a private city view. A custom bronze staircase leads to an observatory level where a game room with a skylight and floor‑to‑ceiling glass walls is shown, followed by a city‑block‑long outdoor oasis on the roof. Near the end she stands in a well‑lit room with a gray sofa, window, artwork and decorative figurines, delivering closing remarks while gesturing. A “click here to subscribe” overlay appears, followed by a pink‑and‑black “Open House” title card over a blurred hallway, ending the segment.

action.detailed: Walk through each room of the penthouse, point out architectural and decorative features such as arched windows, marble fireplace, terraces and skyline views, and describe them to the camera while moving between spaces.
action.actor: Mara Flash Blum, the female real‑estate agent presenting the property

summary.brief: A realtor in a red dress walks through a luxurious New York penthouse, showcasing its rooms, design details and city views.
summary.detailed: The video opens with an Open House graphic and exterior shots of a tall New York building on a bright day. A woman in a red dress enters a grand living area with soaring arched windows, a book‑matched marble fireplace flanked by Italian marble, chevron‑patterned flooring and decorative gargoyles. She moves to a pass‑through fireplace and an elegant dining space illuminated by a distinctive Fendi chandelier. The tour continues through a kitchen, then into the master suite that includes a bedroom, a sitting lounge and a sumptuous bathroom with a steam shower, marble vanities, a soaking tub and a bronze casement window. A custom bronze staircase leads upward to an observatory level that houses a game room with a skylight and glass walls. The camera follows her onto an expansive rooftop terrace and outdoor oasis, where sofas, a piano and panoramic views of the Empire State Building and surrounding skyline are displayed. Throughout the tour she walks, gestures and points to architectural and decorative features while soft music plays in the background.

summary.brief: A woman in a red dress tours a Manhattan penthouse, moving through its rooms while the camera highlights interior details and city vistas.
summary.detailed: The segment opens with low‑angle and aerial shots of a gray‑façade building and the surrounding New York skyline, followed by a street view that includes a passing taxi and busy downtown traffic. The view then cuts inside the penthouse where a woman in a red dress stands in a spacious living area. She addresses the camera and gestures toward a marble‑topped fireplace, marble walls, a grand piano, and a pair of chairs arranged around the fire. The camera pans past arch‑style windows that frame the city, including a view of the Empire State Building. She moves to the kitchen and dining space, where a black glass table is surrounded by colorful upholstered chairs beneath a chandelier of clear glass circles, and large arched windows again showcase the skyline. The tour continues through a bedroom with a large bed, gray pillows and a rug, then into a bathroom featuring a marble tub, shower and vanity. She ascends a polished wooden staircase with glass railings, steps onto a balcony and then a rooftop terrace, repeatedly gesturing toward the panoramic city view. Intermittent cuts show additional amenities such as a foosball table, a black leather couch, a green plant, a mirror, and other decorative details, all set to upbeat background music.

	+ The word "Open" is in pink cursive font, while "HOUSE" is in gray block letters.
	+ The title is centered at the top of the image.
* **Background**
	+ The background of the image is a light beige color.
	+ There is a thin white border around the edge of the image.
* **Copyright Information**
	+ The copyright information is located at the bottom of the image.
	+ It reads "©LXTV/NBC UNIVERSAL, LLC 2019" in small gray text.

Overall, the image effectively promotes the open house event and provides essential information about it. The use of a light beige background and a thin white border creates a clean and simple design that draws attention to the title and copyright information.

The bedroom or dressing room  has 2 arched windows  on the back wall, with a dark colored full-size bed, a side table with a lamp, and several throw pillows on the bed. There is a large rectangular mirror on the left wall and a hallway out to another room leading to a dresser, chair, and a mirror.  On the back wall, there is a long black and white wall-to-wall mirror.
There is also a shower and a bathtub set against the back wall.  This includes 2 long mirror panels and a glass floor panel.  The bathtub is white and in the center, while the shower has a glass and steel frame.  There are also two shower heads and some decorative items on the left side.
The bathroom includes the glass shower area and a white bathtub. There is also a faucet above the tub, while the shower has a stainless steel frame and two shower heads.  There are some towels next to the bathtub and shower, including a purple bath mat, orange towels, and a pink and purple bath mat.  These items are resting on a marble wall that extends over the tub and shower area.
The second room is a white bedroom with 2 arched windows on the back wall and a gray upholstered bed with 8 throw pillows.  The walls are painted white and the ceiling is painted gray.  This room has a large white bed, a black frame with a mirror on the wall, and a white rug in front of the windows.
The third room is the living room and a bedroom. It has a black couch with white cushions, two end tables, one of which has a book and picture frame on it. There is also a white chair, a glass table between the sofa and chair, and a carpet with orange ottomans  on top. The fourth room is a bedroom and sits of a large white bathtub with a silver faucet and a shower with stainless steel walls and 2 showerheads. There are two large windows in the back wall and a large black and white mirror on the wall to the left. The walls are painted white and the ceiling is painted gray.

summary_sent_to_llm.root_summary: The video opens with an “Open House” logo over a city photograph, then introduces Mara Flash Blum of Sotheby’s International Realty. Near the end she stands in a well‑lit room with a gray sofa, window, artwork and decorative figurines, delivering closing remarks while gesturing. llm.system_prompt:
You evaluate YouTube videos for a video-understanding benchmark.

You will be given an Action100M-style summary of one video: title, description,
a hierarchical GPT-written summary of the whole video, and a deduplicated list
of action labels extracted at multiple levels of the video.

Your job is to judge:

1) DOMAINS — does this video clearly belong to any of these target domains?
   - "kitchen": a person preparing food in a kitchen-like setting
     (cooking, baking, food prep — NOT eating reviews, NOT pet-food prep,
     NOT food-product unboxing, NOT restaurant vlogs).
   - "manipulation": a person performing hand-object manipulation tasks
     with clear physical goals: assembly/disassembly, repair, crafting,
     tool use, packing, sorting. The video must show clear procedural
     manipulation, NOT just incidental hand movement (e.g. a vlog where
     someone holds things while talking does NOT count).
   - "navigation": the camera moves through a physical environment as an
     agent traverses space — first-person walking tours (museum, store,
     home, city street), driving / cycling / hiking POV footage, drone
     fly-throughs of indoor or outdoor scenes, room/house walkthroughs.
     The camera's translation through the environment IS the main content.
     Does NOT count: a stationary tripod with someone talking; a tutorial
     filmed in one place; b-roll where the camera only pans or zooms but
     does not translate; sports footage where the player moves but the
     camera stays put.
   A video can match zero, one, or multiple domains. Be strict — when in
   doubt, say "neither".

2) NUM_DISTINCT_EVENTS — count the number of *semantically distinct*
   sub-events (procedural steps) you see in the action list. Merge
   paraphrases of the same step into one. Ignore generic narration steps
   like "speak to camera" or "display title".

3) IS_GOOD_CANDIDATE — true only if BOTH:
   - at least one target domain matches
   - num_distinct_events > 3 (the video shows a real multi-step procedure)

Always return strict JSON in the requested schema.
